Sleek corporate audio logo, smooth synth pad swell with two crisp digital chime notes and a cash register ding, 3 seconds, clean
[warm] You're listening to Boscali Republic Radio. From the hills to the harbor... this is your republic, on the air.
Ninety-one point four, Boscali Republic Radio. Free voices, open skies. Stay tuned.

[relaxed] Good to have you with us. The ferries are running again out of the western hall, the bakers on Quay Street have their ovens lit, and somewhere over the ridge our pilots are keeping the morning quiet. Let's keep it that way. Here's some music.

[thoughtful] A listener wrote in today. Her son flies out of the coastal strip, and she wanted him to know the lemon tree finally fruited. [chuckles] So, pilot, wherever you are... the lemons are in. Come home and eat one.

Quick word from the harbor master: the relief convoy cleared the breakwater twenty minutes ago, every truck accounted for. Thank you to the drivers, the dockhands, and whoever made the coffee. This one's for you.
[softly] It's late. The city's dark on purpose tonight, curtains drawn, streetlights off. If you can hear jets, that's ours. Breathe easy, keep the radio low, and stay with me a while.

[upbeat] Traffic and weather together: the south bridge is open to civilian traffic after inspection, the coast road is slow past the checkpoint, and the clouds are breaking up by noon. Good flying weather. Good drying weather too. Here we go.
[cheerful] Harborline Ferries! Still sailing, still smiling. Daily crossings to the islands, children under twelve ride free, and yes... we've repaired the snack bar. Harborline. We'll get you there.
Your savings build more than a future. They build bridges, clinics and runways. Republic Savings Bonds, available at every post office. Invest in the coast you love.
[earnest] The western ferry hall is collecting blood donations every day this week, eight to eight. It takes fifteen minutes. Bring a friend. Bring a sandwich. Leave a hero.

This is the Republic news desk. The Assembly has voted to extend emergency fuel rationing for another thirty days. Civil defense reminds residents that shelters in the old market district are open overnight. Our forces report the northern air corridor remains contested. More on the hour.

Headlines. Engineers have restored power to most of the harbor district. The election office confirms polling will go ahead as planned. And air defense crews were credited this morning with turning back a raid on the coastal highway. That's the news. Back to music.
[firm] This is PALA State Radio. The voice of the Directorate. Order. Labor. Victory.
[measured] State Radio. Broadcasting on all authorized frequencies. Unauthorized receivers must be registered with the district office.

[stern] Good morning, citizens. Production on the northern rail line exceeded quota for the ninth consecutive week. The Directorate extends its gratitude. Gratitude is not a reason to slow down. The anthem of labor follows.

[measured] The military council reminds all listeners that rumors are a weapon of the enemy. If you hear a rumor, do not repeat it. Write it down. Bring it to your block warden. That is how rumors end.
Curfew begins at the second siren. Windows will be covered. Lights will be extinguished. Children will be indoors. Those who comply have nothing to fear. Music for the evening shift.
[quietly] To the pilots of the People's Air Arm, flying tonight above the eastern provinces. The nation sleeps because you do not. Return with honor. Return with victory.

[proud] A letter from Factory Seven. The workers there have pledged an extra shift each week, without pay, for the defense fund. The Directorate notes this example. The Directorate notes all examples.

Attention. Ration coupons for the new period may be collected at district halls beginning tomorrow. Bring your labor card and your residence permit. Coupons lost will not be replaced. Thank you for your discipline.
[pleasant] Victory Tea. Brewed from the finest state plantations. Enough to share, never enough to waste. Victory Tea. Taste the effort.

Citizens are reminded that listening to foreign broadcasts is an offense against the state. If you have tuned to such a frequency by accident, return to this frequency at once. You have done so. Thank you.

State bulletin. The People's forces have advanced along the eastern front and secured the river crossings. Enemy air activity was repelled with heavy losses. The Directorate denies all reports of fuel shortages. There are no shortages.
State bulletin. Travel permits are now required at all eastern checkpoints. Factory shifts will report one hour before dawn. Do not approach restricted airfields. That concludes the bulletin.
[energetic] Good morning, flight line! This is Base Broadcast, the Boscali Defense Forces network, coming at you from a hardened shelter near you!
[upbeat] Base Broadcast. Keeping the crews awake since... well, since the coffee ran out. BDF radio, on the air.
[cheerful] Rise and shine, people! Ground crews on hardstand four, the chief says you're doing great, and also that somebody left a wrench in a wheel well again. Find your wrench. Here's a song.
Shout out to the tanker crews, flying lazy circles so the rest of us can fly angry ones. You are the gas station in the sky, and we love you. Next up.
[laughs] Mess hall update. Tonight's special is... it's the stew. It's always the stew. Eat the stew, it's good for morale, or so the cook keeps telling me with a very large ladle.
[calmer] Night crews, this one's for you. Quiet ramp, cold engines, and a long way till breakfast. If you're up there right now with your lights off... we've got the kettle on for when you land.
Weather for the flyboys and flygirls: scattered cloud at three thousand, winds light from the sea, visibility great. In other words... no excuses. Let's go.
A message from your flight safety office. Foreign object debris kills engines. A single bolt on the taxiway can ground a jet for a week. Walk the line. Pick it up. Every time.
Loose lips sink ships... and they shoot down jets. Don't post your sortie times. Don't talk shop in town. Radio discipline starts on the ground.
[warm] When was the last time you wrote home? The base post office sends free letters to family every Tuesday. It takes five minutes, and it means everything. Write home.

Forces news. Air defense crews downed two enemy aircraft over the coastal highway overnight. Engineers report the forward strip is open for recovery traffic. All personnel: the revised duty roster is posted in the ready room.
Forces news. Resupply convoys reached the northern bases on schedule. Medical teams remain on immediate standby. And command reminds all pilots to check in with the tower before crossing the active.
[firm] People's Armed Forces Network. Discipline is strength. Strength is victory.
This is the Armed Forces Network of the People's Air Arm. Maintain silence on operational channels.
[measured] Good morning, comrades of the air regiments. The political officer reminds you: an aircraft is the property of the people. Return it in the condition in which it was issued. Music.
Congratulations to the third squadron, whose maintenance crews achieved full readiness for the month. Their names will be read at evening assembly. Yours could be next.
[dry] Mess hall announcement. The bread ration is unchanged. The soup ration is unchanged. Morale... is unchanged. Excellent. Carry on.
[quietly] To the night interceptor crews: the enemy believes darkness protects him. Show him otherwise. The regiment is watching. The nation is listening.
Weather for today's sorties. Cloud at three thousand. Wind from the east. Conditions are acceptable. Conditions are always acceptable.
Attention all personnel. A shelter drill will be conducted at the second siren. Proceed to your assigned bunker in an orderly fashion. Lateness will be recorded.
Vigilance notice. Report any personnel who speak with civilians about aircraft, routes or schedules. Silence protects the regiment.
Fuel is victory. Every liter saved on the ground is a liter in the sky. Ground vehicles will not idle. Thank you for your discipline.

Regiment bulletin. People's interceptors destroyed four enemy aircraft over the eastern provinces. The forward airfield has been reinforced. Pilots will attend the political lecture at nineteen hundred.
Regiment bulletin. The enemy's so-called republic continues to spread lies on foreign frequencies. Do not listen. If you have listened, report it. That is all.
[smooth] You're tuned to Contractor Net. Operational radio for licensed personnel. Your contract. Your performance. Your bonus.
Contractor Net. No flag, no side, no static. Thank you for flying with us.
[pleasant] Good morning, contractors. A reminder that today's sorties are billed per target, not per hour, so please... try to be efficient. Here's something to fly to.
Congratulations to the pilots of flight two, who closed a contract with zero airframe losses this week. Your performance bonus has been processed. Accounting says hello.
[light] Human resources would like to remind everyone that ejection seats are company property. If you use one, please fill out form seven-B. In triplicate. Thank you.
[calm] For those flying tonight: both sides are shooting, neither side is paying overtime, and you are very good at your job. Stay professional. Stay alive. Stay billable.
Market update. Fuel is up, munitions are up, and demand for your services... is way up. It's a good time to be neutral. Music.
[confident] Skyguard Insurance. Because the enemy doesn't care about your deductible. Hull cover, pilot cover, and our famous no-questions ejection plan. Skyguard. Fly uninsured? Never.
Meridian Logistics. Fuel, ordnance and spare parts, delivered to any strip, any side, any time. Payment on delivery. Discretion included.
Tired of flags? Tired of anthems? Contractor Net is hiring experienced pilots. Competitive rates. Flexible loyalties. Apply at your nearest hangar.

Market wire. The Republic and the State have both posted new contracts this morning. Air superiority rates are up twelve percent. Ground attack is steady. Please check the job board before your next sortie.
Market wire. Insurance premiums over the contested corridor have doubled. Management recommends flying above the weather and below the radar. Not at the same time.
